items.prompt: Assess how far the abolitionist movement fostered change in America between 1830 and 1860.
items.original_prompt: Evaluate the extent to which the abolitionist movement fostered change in America from 1830 to 1860.

exemplar.thesis: The abolitionist movement forced slavery onto the national agenda and reshaped politics, building mass antislavery sentiment and new political organizations - though it freed few enslaved people directly before the Civil War.
evidence: William Lloyd Garrison's Liberator (1831) and the American Anti-Slavery Society spread immediatist abolitionism through print and petition campaigns
The Underground Railroad and slave narratives (e.g., Frederick Douglass) made slavery's horrors concrete for northern audiences
Political impact: abolitionism fed the Liberty Party, Free Soil Party, and the Republican Party, while the gag rule and mob violence showed fierce resistance
